content.comment_body: I'm trying to measure a high frequency input (on I4) provided by a 24V flow meter within a water system circuit. The flow meter has a paddlewheel, which in my setup generates frequencies between 0 and 100Hz. To display the flow rate, I tested using both a threshold trigger and an up/down counter. When setting the input manually, I noticed that the threshold trigger outputs match the input frequency, but the up/down counter consistently gives a lower value. The discrepancy is over 10% at lower frequencies and less at higher frequencies. Given the magnitude of the difference, I'm suspecting an issue with my flow chart setup. Any thoughts?
Are you referring to the difference observed in simulation? If so, don't worry too much—simulation doesn't always reflect actual behavior.
Yes, thanks for clarifying. You were correct; there's no difference when using a live input.

analysis.insight_summary: Users identified inconsistencies between threshold trigger and up/down counter functions when measuring frequency inputs from a flow meter using [company_name] automation hardware. The primary concern was inaccurate readings at lower frequencies suggesting a possible configuration error. However, it was determined that these discrepancies were only present during simulation and not with actual live inputs, highlighting limitations of the simulation environment in reliably replicating real-world behavior.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect threshold trigger and up/down counter function blocks to deliver precise and consistent frequency measurements in both simulation and real operational conditions.
